structure: stand-up anecdote with plausible cartoon causality (KayfabeTip 1: therefore/but, never and-then, not verbatim): the action figure tells how the kid who owns him ran a wrestling federation in the living room; every card is the next caused or twisted event (sister, mom, dog, cousin); callbacks dog -> real injury, arm -> outro
synopsis: A spoken-word number from a card deck about the psychology of professional wrestling. It is performed by a toy wrestling figure inside its toy box, for whoever happens to be there.
bestOfReason: 1-4: the heads as gimmicks, the sister as crowd, the jobber is his own head.
9, 13, 14, 11: learning to sell, noise, mom's ban, the sister oversells.
30, 31, 53: empty house, the dog as crowd track, the cousin as smark.
35, 55: the dog's real bite and the family's silence.

cues.cue: plastic click at every head swap

beats: Big Bad Brain Wrestling: every move a lie, every bruise for real.
The kid who owns me got me for his birthday: four heads, one body, a cardboard ring.

beats.pre: First he clicks on the golden head:
beats.text: The Babyface, high-flying moves; audiences cheer, a slave to approval.

beats.pre: His sister yawns, so he clicks the sneer:
beats.text: The Heel, eye pokes; if they aren't booing, you aren't doing your job.

beats.pre: Now she cheers for the wrong one:
beats.text: The Tweener, you don't ask for it, so they want you more.

beats.pre: Somebody has to lose. Guess which head:
beats.text: The Jobber, isolated and picked apart; you exist to make the other guy look good.

beats.pre: Losing hurts, so I learn to fake it:
beats.text: The Master Seller, reel back, limp to the ring, make them believe.
The Thigh Slap, a loud sound suggests high impact; an audio lie.

beats.pre: Mom bans slapping, so we stomp:
The sister tries it and lands in the fish tank:
beats.text: The Oversell Clown, flying backwards from a gentle tap.

beats.pre: Meanwhile the kid writes every ending on the cereal box:
beats.text: The Booker, spider in suit; the ending is pre-planned, you are just a puppet.

beats.pre: He invites the whole class. Nobody comes:
beats.text: The Empty Arena, pausing for a pop that never comes.

beats.pre: So he records the dog barking and plays it back:
beats.text: The Green Screen Crowd, audio sweetening on a lie.

beats.pre: His cousin reviews the show online, never once picked me up:
beats.text: The Internet Smark, psychology without ever taking a bump.

beats.pre: But the dog wants a real match. One bite, no arm:
beats.text: The Real Injury, unplanned; the crowd goes nuts because it's real.

beats.pre: Mom says we never speak of the arm:
beats.text: The Kayfabe Police, keep the secrets secret, or get fired.

beats.pre: One arm left, so the kid books the big finish:
beats.text: The Finisher, the Leg Drop; if this hits, go home.

beats.pre: It hits. The sister counts very slowly:
beats.text: The False Finish, the art of the near-fall.

beats.pre: At Christmas a new figure arrives:
beats.text: The Retirement Match, rising, and falling; see you next season.

beats: Back in the drawer: four heads, one arm. Every bruise for real.
